R011.fact: For the Fourier multiplier S_t of D005 and every real s, S_t is a linear isometry on H^s, S_t S_r=S_(t+r), and t -> S_t f is continuous in H^s for each f in H^s. For strong continuity approximate f by a polynomial: the two tail terms are bounded by twice the approximation error, and the finitely many polynomial coefficients depend continuously on time. R011.justification: The reverse triangle inequality makes the norm continuous. A continuous real function on a compact interval attains its extrema. Under L2 its nonempty level set at 1 is closed and compact, hence has a least time, positive because g(0)=0. Any earlier value greater than 1 would produce an earlier value 1 by the intermediate value theorem. If the level set is empty, the same theorem rules out values above 1; compactness then makes the attained maximum strictly less than 1. argument.text: H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. Fix a0 and temporarily assume L1: a0 is real, mean-zero, in H^gamma and ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R. Set U0(x)=-a0(-x), so hat U0(k)=-hat a0(-k). It is real and mean-zero and preserves all Fourier Sobolev norms. In particular ||U0||_(dot H^gamma)<=R and ||U0||_2<=R. Apply E001 with s=gamma,Q=T,U_0=U0. Its hypotheses hold by these norm facts and H001-H002. It supplies a unique continuous source flow U, a uniform homogeneous bound depending only on T,gamma,R, and smooth-approximation construction. Record its existence as F001.

produces.statement: There exists the unique source solution with initial datum U0 on [0,T], continuous in dot H^gamma, bounded there by a constant depending only on T,gamma,R, constructed by smooth approximation.

argument.text: Choose U from F001 and set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). For smooth solutions u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx at (t,-x), so u_t+u_xxx=-UU_x=u*u_x=(1/2)partial_x(u^2). The same equality follows distributionally by the reflection change of variables for the limiting solution. Fourier coefficients satisfy hat u(t)(k)=-hat U(t)(-k), hence all Sobolev norms, zero mean and reality are preserved. The comparison ||u||_(H^gamma)<=2^(gamma/2)||U||_(dot H^gamma) gives a bound A(T,gamma,R). Finite Fourier norm sums pass to the limit under smooth approximation, and their supremum gives the full bound; continuity gives it for every time. Uniqueness follows by applying the inverse reflection to two solutions, using the source coefficient formulation, equivalent to the distributional equation for continuous L^2 paths by testing each Fourier mode. Set v=S_(-t)u. Unit-modulus multipliers preserve its H^gamma norm. Differentiation for smooth data gives v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v).

produces.statement: Under L1 the exact u exists uniquely, sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R), v=S_(-t)u has the same bound, and for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v).

argument.text: For the smooth-data clause, temporarily assume L3: a0 is smooth. Apply E001 at every positive integer regularity s, with this same U0. Its finite higher norms and uniqueness make all these solutions coincide with U. Thus u is spatially smooth, and the equation supplies its time smoothness. Discharge L3 to obtain that conditional clause, and discharge L1 to obtain the stated assertion for every a0 in the ball. For the pairwise assertion fix arbitrary a0,b0 and temporarily assume L2: they are real mean-zero L^2 data whose norms sum to at most 2*R. Define W0=-b0(-x). E001 with s=0,Q=T supplies the source L^2 flows for each of U0,W0. Apply E002 with Q=T,theta=0,B0=2*R to those flows. Their zero mean, reality and norm sum are unchanged by reflection; theta=0 lies in (-1,0]. Its source common untwisting multiplier is an L^2 isometry, so E002 and reflection give sup||u_a0-u_b0||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. This includes the original H^gamma ball since each norm is <=R. Discharge L2. The constructions and bounds hold for every chosen datum; M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A. This proves the output assertion.

argument.text: Fix tau>0, alpha,beta real. If either phase vanishes its exponential is 1 and the covariance is zero. In the remaining case assume L1: alpha*beta!=0. Define h(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-Mavg_tau(exp(-i*alpha*.)). Then eta=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau h(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The elementary integral estimate |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha||s-r| gives |h(s)|<=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau |alpha||s-r|dr<=tau|alpha|. Consequently |eta|<=tau|alpha|. At s=0,tau the sharper integrals are each tau|alpha|/2, so |h(0)|+|h(tau)|<=tau|alpha|; also integral_0^tau|h'(s)|ds=tau|alpha|.

produces.statement: Under L1, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau|alpha| and |h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral_0^tau|h'|<=2*tau|alpha|.

argument.text: Integration by parts against exp(-i*beta*s), which has nonzero derivative factor -i*beta under L1, gives |eta|<= (|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta| by F001. The defining covariance is symmetric in alpha,beta; repeating both estimates with the phases interchanged gives |eta|<=tau|beta| and |eta|<=2|beta/alpha|. Take their minima, discharge L1, and include the zero-phase case already calculated. Universal introduction proves the output assertion.

argument.text: For the pointwise assertions fix integers a,b,c,d and assume L1: abcd!=0 and a+b+c+d=0. Order their magnitudes as N1>=N2>=N3>=N4. The largest is bounded by the sum of the other three, so N1<=3*N2. Put A0=|ab|, B0=|cd|. If d is among the two largest, min(A0/B0,B0/A0)<=1 and 1/|d|<=1/N3. If not, the largest two are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, use B0/A0 to bound the desired expression by |c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio lies in [1/3,3]. Therefore the expression is at most 3*min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3: use the first alternative if |d|>=|b| and the second otherwise. The case b,c is identical after swapping a,b. This proves the first majorant.

produces.statement: Under L1, N1<=3*N2 and (1/|d|)min(A0/B0,B0/A0)<=3/N3.

argument.text: For the second majorant, if the two largest are in the same pair of (a,b),(c,d), the other pair sums to magnitude at most 2*N3. Since a+b=-(c+d), |a+b|/max(A0,B0)<=2*N3/(N1*N2)<=2/N3. If they lie in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, whence max(A0,B0)>=N2*N3; also |a+b|<=2*N1<=6*N2 by F001. The quotient is <=6/N3. Any ordering of ties is covered. Discharge L1; these are the claimed conditional pointwise statements for all such frequencies.

Fix four nonnegative ell^2 sequences x_r. First restrict all of them to finitely many frequencies. Decompose each into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, and let Xshell_(r,j) be its ell^2 norm there. Fix one of the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices j1>=j2>=j3>=j4, permuting the sequence labels accordingly. A nonzero zero-sum interaction requires j1-j2<=2, since otherwise the largest magnitude would exceed the sum of the other three. For each fixed pair of the two smaller frequencies, sum the two larger-frequency sequences subject to their prescribed sum. Cauchy-Schwarz, applied to a translated reflection, bounds that sum by their shell ell^2 norm product. A shell contains at most 2^(j+1) integers, so summing each smaller sequence in ell^1 costs at most C*2^(j/2) times its ell^2 norm. Thus the shell contribution without the weight is <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr). On that shell N3>=2^j3, so the weight leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2).

produces.statement: For every ordered four-shell zero-sum interaction j1>=j2>=j3>=j4, its weighted contribution is <=C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr), and j1-j2 is in {0,1,2}.

argument.text: For each q in {0,1,2}, set j1=J,j2=J-q. Drop the upper restrictions on the smaller shells; nonnegativity increases the sum. F002 bounds the ordered contribution by C*(sum_J Xshell_(1,J)*Xshell_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m>=0)2^(-(ell-m)/2)*Xshell_(3,ell)*Xshell_(4,m)). The first factor is at most ||Xshell_1||_ell2||Xshell_2||_ell2. Set r=ell-m; for each r the second correlation is at most ||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2 by Cauchy-Schwarz, so the second factor is at most sum_(r>=0)2^(-r/2)||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2=||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2/(1-2^(-1/2)). Shell disjointness identifies each shell-norm ell^2 norm with ||x_r||_ell2. Sum over 24 orderings and three offsets. This proves the finite bound with an absolute constant.

produces.statement: For the finite restrictions of the current nonnegative ell^2 sequences, sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0)x_1(a)x_2(b)x_3(c)x_4(d)/N3(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_(r=1)^4||x_r||_ell2, with absolute C independent of the supports; N3 is the third largest magnitude in the summand.

argument.text: For arbitrary nonnegative ell^2 sequences restrict all inputs to |k|<=m and apply F003. Their norms are bounded by the full norms. Every finite subset of interactions is included in some such restriction, so the infinite positive sum, defined as the supremum over finite subsums, has the same bound. Restricting to any subset only decreases that nonnegative sum. Together with the pointwise assertions this proves the output assertion without exchanging conditionally convergent sums.

argument.text: Dualize the Fourier coefficients of Rem against a finitely supported unit ell^2 sequence. After absolute values, use F001 and N003 with x_1(a)=|a|^sigma|hat f_1(a)| and likewise for slots 2 and 3; take x_4(d) to be the modulus of the dual coefficient at -d. Their norms are bounded by the three H^sigma norms and the unit dual norm. The factor exp(-i*t0*Phi) has modulus one, and the prefactor in Rem is tau/18. Thus ||Rem||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma). A multiplier of modulus <=1 only decreases the absolute majorant, so the same proof covers every stated restriction.

produces.statement: For the mean-zero polynomial inputs, ||Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_(j=1)^3||f_j||_(H^sigma), uniformly in their supports, t0 and tau, including any fixed interaction multiplier of modulus <=1.

argument.text: Approximate each mean-zero H^sigma input by its finite Fourier projections. The trilinear bound F002 and the three-term telescoping difference bound show that the outputs are Cauchy in the complete L^2 space, independently of the chosen approximations. This defines a unique bounded trilinear extension and retains the inequality. For smooth inputs it coincides with the original absolutely convergent Fourier expression. At sigma=0 this supplies in particular an L^2-by-L^2-by-L^2 bound C*tau.

produces.statement: For every exponent rho in [0,1], Rem_(t0,tau) has a unique bounded trilinear extension to the mean-zero H^rho inputs g_1,g_2,g_3, with ||Rem_(t0,tau)(g_1,g_2,g_3)||_2<=C_rho*tau^(1+rho)*product_j||g_j||_(H^rho). The same bound holds with any fixed extra multiplier of modulus <=1, and at rho=0 it is C*tau times the product of L^2 norms.

argument.text: For the final clause fix f,w,M0 and temporarily assume L1: 0<sigma<=1,0<tau<=1,w in mean-zero H^sigma with ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M0, f in mean-zero L^2, and delta=||f-w||_2<=1. Apply F003 with exponent sigma to (w,w,w). Expand Rem(f,f,f)-Rem(w,w,w) as Rem(f-w,f,f)+Rem(w,f-w,f)+Rem(w,w,f-w) and apply F003 with exponent zero to each term. The difference is bounded by C*tau*delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Since ||f||_2<=M0+1, this yields C_(sigma,M0)*tau*(tau^sigma+delta). Discharge L1 and quantify all data. This proves the output assertion.

argument.text: For any mean-zero L^2 f, Cauchy-Schwarz in its Fourier series gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2, and coefficient weights give ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. For a general H^1 function its mean plus this estimate for its derivative gives ||A0||_infinity<=C||A0||_(H^1). The product rule then gives ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Apply it to S_t Dinv f and S_t Dinv g and use S_t isometric and P contractive to obtain ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. Each assertion is quantified over inputs in its indicated space.

argument.text: For L^2 f,g, every Fourier coefficient of the product (S_t f)(S_t g) has modulus <=||f||_2||g||_2 by Cauchy-Schwarz in the convolution. Hence ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0) k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), a finite sum because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum k^(-2) proves ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1), so ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2. Finally J_t(A0,g) is a product of S_t Dinv A0 in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infinity, followed by contractions, so its L^2 norm is <=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2 by F001. Approximation by polynomials and these continuous bilinear bounds justify the products and their extensions.

argument.text: For the normal-form clause take smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b]. At k!=0 the coefficient of J_t is sum_(r+s=k) exp(-i*t*3*k*r*s)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiating the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients. Therefore d_t J_t(f,g)=3*B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smooth spatial Fourier series and all derivatives used here converge absolutely, so differentiation and integration are legitimate. Integration gives the displayed two-endpoint normal form. For piecewise smooth continuous paths apply this on each subinterval; intermediate J endpoint values cancel because the paths are continuous.

argument.text: Symmetry of J is immediate from the product formula. For constant f,g, integrate F003 and multiply by 1/2 to obtain Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_a^t. This establishes every identity asserted in the output assertion.

argument.text: Apply E003 on I=[a,b]. For its first assertion take alpha=0 and any slot i in {1,2,3}. The stated spatially smooth paths, continuous and piecewise smooth in time on a finite compact partition, have bounded L2 norms and bounded piecewise H^(-pstar) derivatives. Integration by parts against a compactly supported smooth scalar time test function on each piece gives their weak derivatives; adjacent endpoint terms cancel by continuity, so there are no jump masses. Thus all three paths satisfy E003's hypotheses. For its second assertion take alpha=sigma, with arbitrary 0<=sigma<=1 and constant H^sigma inputs; their weak derivatives are zero. Put c0=sqrt(2*pi). Every source spatial norm and source X norm is c0 times the corresponding normalized norm. Dividing the source trilinear inequalities by c0 multiplies each constant by c0^2 and preserves time powers, all three negative-norm slots, and uniformity in a,b and the inputs. These are the two asserted normalized Ctri bounds. For completeness, bounded multilinear extensions used here and below follow by approximating inputs in their controlling norms: expand a difference of multilinear outputs as a sum of terms each containing one input difference. The bounds make outputs Cauchy and their limits independent of the approximants, with the same bound. Sobolev Fourier truncations are dense by convergence of the defining weighted square sums, and deleting the zero mode preserves mean zero. This gives the constant-input extensions; for path inputs the same argument gives the extension to the closure of the stated initial domain in its controlling X norm, without assuming density in the entire X space.

argument.text: H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Define a_gamma by the displayed three-case formula; the three cases give a_gamma in [0,1). First establish the required Sobolev comparison directly from D003: for real q<=r and any u in H^r, each weight (1+k^2)^q is at most (1+k^2)^r. Summing the weighted squared coefficients gives ||u||_(H^q)<=||u||_(H^r), with the identity inclusion on Fourier coefficients. For completions this follows first for Fourier truncations and then by their norm convergence; for the nonnegative exponents used here these inclusions identify the same L2 function. For 0<gamma<1/2 or 1/2<gamma<=1, E005 with sigma=gamma has source a(sigma)=a_gamma and directly gives the product inequality. At gamma=1/2, do not prescribe a numerical source epsilon. E005's 'any sufficiently small positive epsilon' means there is a positive threshold below which all positive choices are permitted; taking half the minimum of such a threshold and 1/8 supplies a permitted epsP with 0<epsP<=1/8. Fix one such epsP independently of f,g. Apply E005 with sigma=1/2 and source a(sigma)=epsP to arbitrary f in H^(1/2) and g in H^(1/8), using the just-proved inclusion H^(1/8) into H^epsP. Its exact conclusion is |f*g|_2<=c_(1/2,epsP)|f|_(1/2)|g|_(epsP), bounded by c_(1/2,epsP)|f|_(1/2)|g|_(1/8). Dividing every bilinear source inequality by c0 changes the constant by c0, and proves F002 with the unchanged a_gamma. The fixed source-dependent epsP is absorbed in C_gamma. No gamma=0 product assertion is needed.

argument.text: First fix a permitted epsF with 0<epsF<=1/8 for E004's sigma=1/2 case. Such a choice exists because E004 allows every sufficiently small fixed positive epsilon: choose half the minimum of a positive admissibility threshold and 1/8. Fix this choice using E004 alone, independently of all stage data; only the gamma=1/2 case uses it. Fix the arbitrary a,tau,t,w,M0 as declared and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. Set wshift=S_a w. The multiplier of S_a has modulus one and is one at frequency zero, so it preserves each H norm and the mean. Its multiplier group law gives B_(a+r)(f,g)=S_(-a)B_r(S_a f,S_a g) for smooth time-independent inputs. Substituting s=a+r in D021 and moving the fixed bounded map S_(-a) through the smooth time integral gives Fstage_(a,t)(w)=S_(-a)Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift), initially for smooth mean-zero w. Apply E004 with sigma=gamma, n=0, timestep tau, s=t-a, f=g=wshift and beta=a_gamma; use epsF at gamma=1/2. Here tau>0 and 0<=t-a<=tau. For gamma<1/2, beta0=2*gamma-3/2 and a_gamma-beta0=2-3*gamma>0; for gamma=1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsF and a_gamma-beta0=5/8+epsF>0; for gamma>1/2 the gap is 1-gamma>=0. In every case a_gamma<=1+gamma. The denominator 1+gamma-beta0 is respectively 5/2-gamma, 2+epsF, and 2, all positive. Thus E004 yields exactly the source powers (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma), (11/8)/(2+epsF), and (1+gamma)/2 in these three cases. Each is at least gamma: in the first case subtracting gamma times the positive denominator from the numerator gives 1/2-gamma/2+gamma^2>0; in the middle case epsF<=1/8 implies (11/8)/(2+epsF)>=11/17>1/2; in the last case 1>=gamma. Since 0<tau<=1, a power at least gamma gives tau to that power at most tau^gamma. Divide the source bilinear estimate by c0, multiplying its constant by c0. Use the isometry S_(-a) and ||wshift||_(H^gamma)=||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 to obtain ||Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_gamma*M0^2*tau^gamma uniformly over a<=t<=a+tau. These calculations first hold on mean-zero trigonometric polynomials; E004 is bilinear, so the difference and completion argument in S001 extends its bounds and the covariance identity to mean-zero H^gamma inputs. To pass the covariance identity, apply it to Fourier truncations and use the bounded S maps on the source and target Sobolev spaces. All constants are independent of a,t,tau and Fourier support. Taking the supremum in t proves F003; the fixed epsF is absorbed in C_gamma.

argument.text: Apply E004 to the same wshift and time parameters with beta=1+gamma, retaining the permitted epsF at gamma=1/2. This is the upper endpoint of [beta0,1+gamma]. The positive denominator was checked in S003 and the numerator 1+gamma-beta is zero, so the source power is zero. After division by c0 the exact estimate is ||Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma||wshift||_(H^gamma)^2. The smooth covariance identity established in S003 and the S isometry give the same bound for Fstage_(a,t)(w); the bilinear difference and Fourier completion argument of S001 extends both this bound and the identity to H^gamma inputs, now with target H^(1+gamma). Under L1 the right side is at most C_gamma*M0^2, uniformly in a,t,tau and Fourier support. Enlarge C_(gamma,M0) to cover this bound and F003 (for example a fixed C_gamma*(1+M0^2)). Discharge L1 into the norm-bound antecedent and universally quantify M0,w,tau,a,t. The two target Sobolev extensions agree as distributions because they arise from the same polynomial truncations and H^(1+gamma) includes continuously in H^(a_gamma) by the Fourier norm comparison proved in S002. With F001 and F002 this proves every clause of the output assertion, including the stated extensions. Neither chosen source epsilon occurs in the public input/output.

argument.text: Fix tau>0. N005 makes Dinv:L^2->H^1 bounded and H^1 an algebra. Therefore Ftau is a continuous quadratic map L^2->H^1. In Htau the first product has factors S_tau Dinv f and Dinv Ftau(f) in H^1; the second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2) and S_tau Dinv f; the third is an H^1 cube followed by Dinv and S; the fourth multiplies S_(s-tau)Dinv2 Ftau(f) by S_s Dinv f in H^1, followed by Dinv2 and S, evaluated at two endpoints. Every coefficient, including 1/tau, is finite at this fixed tau. Hence all four terms, Ftau and Psi_tau are continuous in L^2. Fourier conjugate symmetry is preserved by S, Dinv, products and real coefficients. Every projected or inverse-derivative term has zero mean, and the unprojected second term of Htau is a scalar times the mean-zero S_tau Dinv f. Thus the update is real and mean-zero. The same formulas preserve spatial smoothness. Finite induction gives the asserted well-defined finite trajectories and continuous dependence at fixed tau.

Expanding J(f,f)-J(w,w) as J(f-w,f)+J(w,f-w) gives sup||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Since a_gamma<1, N006 now yields sup(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. argument.text: Set Astage=Fstage_(a,t)(w) and Dstage=F-Astage. Apply the product bound in N006 to partial_x(S_t Astage) and S_t Astage, using the H^(1+gamma) and H^(a_gamma) stage bounds. It gives ||partial_x[(S_t Astage)^2]||_2<=2*C_gamma||Astage||_(H^(1+gamma))||Astage||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma. The difference of squares is (S_t Dstage)*S_t(F+Astage). The H^1 algebra estimate in N005 and F001 give its derivative norm <=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Therefore sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Integrating yields sup||Q||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. N004 with exponent gamma and the current f,w then bounds Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f) by the same quantity, so ||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

For the other product use ||f-w||_2||S_t F||_infinity<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta by the uniform H^1 stage bound and N005. Thus sup||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Differentiating the definition Y=Cst+Q-((t-a)/tau)W gives Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau. N005, F002 and this asymmetric product estimate give sup||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. As Y(a)=0, integration gives sup||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: Apply the normal form of N005 to Cst=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s))ds, with f constant, F(a)=0 and F'=(1/2)B(f,f). Symmetry and the J(B,h)-to-Ctri identity give exactly Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f). Its J term is O(q) in L^2 by N005 and F001. In its Ctri term use N006 with exponent gamma on (w,w,w) to get O(tau^gamma). Expand the difference from (f,f,f) into three trilinear differences and use N006 with exponent zero on each; their size is O(delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2). Thus sup||Cst||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. With F002 in Y=Cst+Q-affine W this gives sup||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f), and sup_I||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: All stage components are mean-zero because B and Rem have zero output mean. N005 gives ||Y'||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y'||_2 and ||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y||_2. argument.text: Collect F001-F005. Discharge L1 and universally quantify all the step data. This proves every clause of the output assertion.

argument.text: H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. First fix a step with the antecedent L1 of N008: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, delta=||f-w||_2<=1, with smooth real mean-zero f,w, M0>=1 and the stated a,tau. Use its tuple and q. Differentiation of Interp gives Vst'=(1/2)B_t(z,z)-W/tau. Since Vst=z+Y, subtraction of (1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst) gives rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau. The residual increment vanishes at a. N008 bounds ||Y||_2 by C*q, ||z||_2 by C and ||W||_2/tau by C*q, with q<=2. N005 thus gives ||rho'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: For the first integral in rho apply N005's normal form to (Y,z). Its boundary J terms are O(tau*q) using ||Dinv Y||_2<=C*tau*q from N008 and bounded ||z||_2. The integral containing Y' is O(tau*q) by the asymmetric J bound and ||Dinv Y'||_2<=C*q. Since z'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), symmetry turns the remaining term into a fixed multiple of Ctri_[a,t](f,f,Y). Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y: N008 gives ||Y||_X<=C*q and ||Y||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q, while f is constant with L^2 norm <=M0+1. Hence this term too is O(tau*q), even on a partial step.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(a<=t<=a+tau)||integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: For integral B(Y,Y), apply the same normal form with Y in both slots. Boundary terms use ||Dinv Y||_2||Y||_2<=C*tau*q^2, and derivative integrals use ||Dinv Y'||_2||Y||_2<=C*q^2 over length tau. Thus it is O(tau*q^2)=O(tau*q) because q<=2. The affine W term is O(tau*q) by N008. Combine with F001-F002 to prove both residual estimates on the whole or any initial part of the step. Discharge L1 and quantify the data.

produces.statement: For every Mbar>=1,a0>=0,0<tau1<=1 and smooth real mean-zero f0,w0 with ||w0||_(H^gamma)<=Mbar and ||f0-w0||_2<=1, let q0=tau1^gamma+||f0-w0||_2 and let Y0,z0,W0,V0 be the corresponding components of Interp_(a0,tau1;f0). Define rho0(t)=-integral_a0^t B_s(Y0,z0)ds-(1/2)integral_a0^t B_s(Y0,Y0)ds-((t-a0)/tau1)W0. On [a0,a0+tau1], V0'=(1/2)B_t(V0,V0)+rho0', rho0'=-B_t(Y0,z0)-(1/2)B_t(Y0,Y0)-W0/tau1, sup||rho0||_2<=C_(gamma,Mbar)*tau1*q0 and ||rho0'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,Mbar)*q0.

argument.text: Now fix a smooth numerical trajectory and exact twisted v and assume L2: sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h<=1 and E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1. N007 gives the continuous interpolation V with grid values v^n. Concatenate the residual increments, obtaining Rres and V'=(1/2)B(V,V)+Rres' stepwise and distributionally. At each intersected step start t_n, delta_n=||v^n-v(t_n)||_2=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I, so its q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I and F003 applies with w=v(t_n),f=v^n. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps; the last can be partial. Sum the step increment bounds to obtain sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). Also sup||Rres'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L2, sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I) and ||Rres'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

argument.text: Under L2, ||v||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0 and ||V||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0+1. Subtract the equations to obtain e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 and F004 imply ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), so ||e||_X has the same bound. The exact equation bounds ||v'||_(H^(-pstar)), and V=v-e then has bounded X norm too, since tau^gamma+E_I<=2. This proves the remaining assertions. Discharge L2 and quantify the trajectory and interval.

locals.declaration: Fix 0<tau<=1, with the smaller final restriction imposed later.
Fix the exact twisted path v.
Fix the interpolation V of the specified numerical trajectory.
Fix a grid starting point a.
Use the concatenated step residual defined by N009.
Fix an arbitrary proof-only threshold N>=2.
Let Hproj be the identity operator minus Lproj.
Choose C0>=1 dominating the finite constants in F005, uniformly over admissible intervals and trajectories.

argument.text: H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. Assume L1: the smooth real mean-zero v satisfies v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and the numerical interpolation V is taken on an interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, E_I<=1. Set e=v-V,g=v-e/2 and take the concatenated Rres from N009. Its conclusions apply to this trajectory and give the accumulated residual and X bounds. In particular e'=B_t(e,g)-Rres', so integration gives e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Also ||e||_X<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||v||_X+||V||_X+||g||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

produces.statement: Under L1, e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)), sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))+||g||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0).

argument.text: Fix N>=2 only in the proof. For each time s, the inverse-product bound of N005 and the Fourier inequality ||Ple_N partial_x^2 A||_2<=N^2||A||_2 give ||Ple_N B_s(e,g)||_2<=C*N^2||e||_2||g||_2. Indeed B_s(e,g)=S_(-s)partial_x^2 Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]. Integrate over length at most h and use bounded ||g||_2 to obtain sup||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, for every N>=2, sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

argument.text: Apply the two-endpoint normal form N005 to F_I. The equations give e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=(1/2)B(v,v)-(1/2)B(e,g)+(1/2)Rres'. In the differentiated J terms, its symmetry and integral J(B,h)=Ctri give Ctri(e,g,g)-(1/2)Ctri(e,g,e)=Ctri(e,g,V), since g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is (1/2)Ctri(v,v,e), and the forcing terms satisfy -J(Rres',g)+(1/2)J(e,Rres')=-J(Rres',V). Multiplication by -1/3 yields F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Both endpoints are retained. Apply the H^1 bound for J in N005: their projections above N are <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I. Continuity of all the paths makes internal endpoints cancel when the normal form is applied stepwise.

produces.statement: Under L1, F_I(t)=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. The sum of the norms of Pgt_N J_t(e,g) and Pgt_N J_a(e,g) is <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I.

argument.text: For any three admissible paths on I, put Lproj=Ple_(N/3),Hproj equal to the identity operator minus Lproj. The telescoping expansion Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)-Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Lproj f_3)=Ctri(Hproj f_1,f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Hproj f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Hproj f_3) places a high input in each term. The all-low term has no output above N because all product frequencies sum. Each projection contracts both components of X and ||Hproj f_i||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||f_i||_2 by Fourier weights. Apply N006 with the negative norm on that particular high slot. This proves ||Pgt_N Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infinity L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e), using F001: their total contribution is <=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, ||Pgt_N Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)||_2+||Pgt_N Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I uniformly for t in I.

argument.text: For the remaining integral in F003 substitute the actual stepwise Rres' formula from N009, and use integral J(B,h)=Ctri from N005 on each intersected step segment. It becomes -Ctri(Y_n,z_n,V)-(1/2)Ctri(Y_n,Y_n,V)-tau^(-1)integral J_s(W_n,V)ds. At that step's start, delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. N008 gives ||Y_n||_X<=C*q_n, ||Y_n||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C and ||W_n||_2<=C*tau*q_n. N006, with the negative norm on Y_n, bounds the first two terms by C*tau*q_n (using q_n<=2 and ||V||_X<=C from F001). The last term is also <=C*tau*q_n by the L^2 J bound from N005. These remain valid upper bounds on a partial final step. At most h/tau+1 steps are met, and q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I. Thus the forcing integral is bounded by C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(t in I)||integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). All constants in this bound and the endpoint, cubic, low-frequency and accumulated residual bounds can be dominated by a single positive constant depending only on gamma,M0, uniformly over admissible trajectories, intervals, timesteps and thresholds N>=2.

argument.text: Combine F003-F005 to obtain sup||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. With F002, the exact error identity and residual bound in F001 give E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. All constants are uniform in the parameters specified in F005.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, with one constant depending only on gamma,M0.

argument.text: Choose C0>=1 dominating these constants from F005-F006, independently of all the particular paths. Define N0=ceil(max(2,16*C0,(16*C0)^(1/pstar))). Then C0*(N0^(-1)+N0^(-pstar))<=1/8<=1/4. Put delta0=min(1,1/(8*C0*(N0^2+3))) and K0=4*C0. If h<=delta0 and tau<=delta0/2, then C0*(N0^2*h+h+tau)<=C0*delta0*(N0^2+3)<=1/8<=1/4. F006 therefore has E_I coefficient at most 1/2. Absorption gives E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+2*C0*(h+tau)*tau^gamma<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. These choices depend only on gamma,M0. Discharge L1, retaining its antecedents in the conditional theorem, and quantify all trajectories, intervals and timesteps. This proves the output assertion.

In particular, record F001: there exists such an A, simultaneously valid for all data in the ball, and smooth data have smooth exact flows.

argument.text: Choose A from F001 and set M0=1+A. Apply N010 with this M0 and the fixed gamma. Its quantitative choices depend only on gamma,M0, so there exist common delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0 for the whole initial-data ball, not for one numerical trajectory. Record this existence as F002.

produces.statement: There exist delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that for every 0<tau<=delta0/2, every smooth exact twisted v with v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and corresponding continuous numerical interpolation V, and every interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point with b-a<=delta0 and sup_I||v-V||_2<=1, one has sup_I||v-V||_2<=2||v(a)-V(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma.

argument.text: Choose delta0,K0 together from F002. Put Bcount=ceil(2*T/delta0)+1, Csm=K0*delta0*(2^Bcount-1), and tausm=min(1,delta0/2,(1/(4*(Csm+1)))^(1/gamma)). These are positive and depend only on T,gamma,R; for tau<=tausm, Csm*tau^gamma<1/4. These choices precede the choice of data and number of steps.

produces.statement: Csm>0,tausm>0 depend only on T,gamma,R, tausm<=min(1,delta0/2), and Csm*tau^gamma<1/4 whenever 0<tau<=tausm.

argument.text: Fix u_0,Lsteps and assume L1: u_0 is smooth, real and mean-zero, ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R, Lsteps is a positive integer, and tau=T/Lsteps<=tausm. Let u be its N001 flow, v=S_(-t)u and V the N007 interpolation of the smooth numerical trajectory; e=v-V is continuous and e(0)=0. The common bound is sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=A<M0 and v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Put mblock=floor(delta0/tau). Since tau<=delta0/2, mblock>=1 and mblock*tau is in [delta0/2,delta0]. Divide the grid into blocks of mblock steps, with a possibly shorter final block. There are at most Bcount blocks. On each block, or its initial part, on which the bootstrap sup||e||_2<=1 holds, F002 and N010 give E_block<=2||e(start)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. Induction from e(0)=0 yields E on block j at most K0*delta0*(2^j-1)*tau^gamma, and hence <=Csm*tau^gamma, as long as the bootstrap is valid. A block truncated inside a step is covered by N010.

produces.statement: Under L1, on every initial interval where sup||e||_2<=1 the complete block induction gives sup||e||_2<=Csm*tau^gamma<1/4, including a final endpoint inside a step.

argument.text: Suppose L2: ||e||_2 reaches 1 somewhere on [0,T]. By continuity and e(0)=0 there is a first such time; the bootstrap is valid up to it. F004, with the last block truncated at that time, gives a bound <1/4, a contradiction. Discharge L2 by classical contradiction. Thus the bootstrap never fails and F004 holds on all [0,T]. N007 gives V(n*tau)=S_(-n*tau)u^n, and S_(n*tau) is unitary, so the grid norm ||e(n*tau)||_2 equals ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2. Discharge L1 and quantify u_0,Lsteps. The constants were chosen first, uniformly, so both full assertions of the output assertion follow.

Since T>0, this tau is positive. N001 supplies its unique exact solution u with the stipulated smooth-approximation meaning. Define u0seq_m=Ple_m u_0. Each is a real mean-zero trigonometric polynomial, its H^gamma norm is <=R, and ||u0seq_m-u_0||_2 tends to zero by convergence of the Fourier norm tails. argument.text: Let useq_m be the exact flows and unumseq_m their numerical trajectories. N001's L^2 continuous dependence, since the initial L^2 norms sum to <=2*R, gives sup_[0,T]||useq_m-u||_2<=K(T,2*R)||u0seq_m-u_0||_2 ->0. No uniform Lipschitz bound for Psi as tau->0 is required: the limit is taken at a fixed timestep, with finite 1/tau coefficients and finitely many iterations.

argument.text: For each m, F002 yields max_n||useq_m(n*tau)-unumseq_m^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Use F003 and continuity of the norm, and then take the maximum over the finite Lsteps+1 points, to pass to the limit. This gives max_n||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. The exact solution is the unique smooth-approximation solution by N001; N007 ensures the rough-data recursion is defined and stays real mean-zero. The constants C,tau_0 are unchanged in this limit and were chosen uniformly before u_0,Lsteps. Discharge L1 and introduce both universal quantifiers. P follows for the entire original ball, with no Fourier support or extra smoothness hypothesis.

full_target:
Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with the standing definitions of Section 2 of the supplied paper.

Use normalized measure dx/(2*pi) on the torus \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/(2*pi \mathbb{Z}). The Fourier coefficient is
\hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx,
and ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s)|\hat f(k)|^2, where <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2).
These spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The normalized L^2 norm is the s=0 norm. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous norm uses |k|^(2s) in place of <k>^(2s). For s>=0,
||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s);
for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s).
Real-valued means \hat f(-k)=overline(\hat f(k)), and mean-zero means \hat f(0)=0.
All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), so \widehat{S_t f}(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)\hat f(k).
Let P_0 be the mean and P=I-P_0. Let D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at k=0; D^(-2)=(D^(-1))^2.
The equation is
u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2),  u(0)=u_0. [Eq. (1)]
The exact solution u is the unique real, mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation and satisfies this equation distributionally.

For a positive integer L and tau=T/L, the fixed time-semidiscrete scheme is u^0=u_0 and
u^(n+1)=S_tau u^n+F_tau(u^n)+H_tau(u^n), 0<=n<L, [Eq. (2)]
where
F_tau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
This is the fixed scheme of the paper's reference [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, every 0<gamma<=1 and every R>0, there exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real, mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(\mathbb{T}) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau_0, this exact fixed scheme satisfies
max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2)<=C*tau^gamma.
The same C and tau_0 apply to the entire stated initial-data ball; no spectral support bound or additional smoothness is a hypothesis.
